title: The storage-nearly-full repair reads two keys hub_readings never emits, so it can never fire
rationale: repairs._storage asks coordinator.readings for `storage_total` and `storage_free`; hub_readings only ever produces `storage_total_gb`, `storage_free_gb` and `storage_used_percent`. Both lookups return None on every poll, `if not total or free is None` is always true, and the function deletes the issue and returns. The only advance warning before loop recording starts silently overwriting the oldest footage is permanently dead. diagnostics.py names this exact near-miss (`storage_total` for `storage_total_gb`) as a bug already fixed elsewhere while this copy was missed. Fix is two key names.

Verified at HEAD b764e98, line numbers unchanged (iteration 1 did not touch repairs.py or status.py).

        issue_id = _issue_id(entry_id, STORAGE_ISSUE)
        # Unknown is not the same as fine. Say nothing rather than guessing.
        if not total or free is None:

        "storage_used_percent": used_percent,

title: The hub_unreachable repair issue can only fire while the hub IS reachable -- it is raised from inside the success path
rationale: repairs.async_check has exactly one call site, near the end of _poll(), after `self._polls += 1`. When the hub is down, _poll() raises UpdateFailed at the activity fetch and never reaches it, so the unreachable issue can never be created during an outage -- which is the only time it is meant to exist. The module docstring names that exact case as its reason for existing. The second-order effect (the notice flashing for one interval at the moment of recovery, because HA only flips last_update_success after _async_update_data returns) follows from HA internals I could not verify locally, but the primary defect does not depend on it. Effort is above the board's 1 because the fix needs a call site that survives a failed poll -- an except/finally in the refresh path, or an async_add_listener -- not just moving one line.

            async_check(self.hass, self.entry.entry_id, self)
        except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - never fail a poll over this

title: Writing a hub setting refreshes the coordinator but not readings, so every control snaps back to its old value for up to a minute
rationale: H500HubControl.apply's comment promises "one poll after the write ... so the new value is not guessed at", but the poll it triggers only re-reads hub_status when `self._polls % self._status_every == 0`, and _status_every is round(60/2)=30 at the default interval. So roughly 29 writes in 30 leave self.readings holding the pre-write value: the LED, loop-recording, auto-upgrade and face-detection switches, the siren volume and duration numbers and the siren-tone select all revert in the frontend and stay reverted until the next scheduled status fetch. siren.py has the same problem on its own two refresh calls. A one-shot "status is due next poll" flag fixes every control at once and adds no hub round trips.
evidence:
Verified at HEAD b764e98, line numbers unchanged.

custom_components/tapo_h500/hub_control.py:37-39 --
        # One poll after the write, not one per call: this hub is easy to
        # overload and the readings all arrive in a single round trip anyway.
        await self.coordinator.async_request_refresh()

but the poll gates the status fetch, coordinator.py:753 --
        if self._polls % self._status_every == 0:

and the divisor is 30 at defaults, coordinator.py:112 --
        self._status_every = max(1, round(STATUS_MAX_AGE / interval))

with const.py:139 `DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL = 2` and const.py:155 `STATUS_MAX_AGE = 60`.

Same defect in the siren, siren.py:84 and siren.py:88 -- both `await self.coordinator.async_request_refresh()` after a write.

The existing test confirms the divisor rather than the consequence, tests/test_coordinator.py:400 --

title: The 60-second poll rebuilds innerHTML wholesale, restarting any open <video> from zero with autoplay
rationale: _load() always calls _render() in its finally, and _render() assigns this._card.innerHTML, destroying and recreating every child element. this._playing survives the reload, so _player() re-emits a brand-new `<video controls autoplay>` -- a user watching or paused mid-clip is yanked back to 0:00 and force-played once a minute, and the scroll position goes with it. The cheap root-cause fix is caching the last rendered HTML string in a field and skipping the assignment when unchanged (never read innerHTML back -- the browser reserializes it), which also fixes every other no-op re-render path.

title: The preview view accepts any start_time, opening an unbounded media session per request and 500ing with a traceback on out-of-range values
rationale: H500PreviewView is the integration's only HTTP endpoint and its only input validation is a sign check. Any authenticated HA user -- or anyone holding one of the 12-hour signed URLs, with no HA credentials at all -- can request an arbitrary timestamp, and every cache miss opens a fresh TCP + digest + AES media session against hardware this project documents as wedging under enough of them. Nothing checks the timestamp corresponds to an indexed clip and there is no negative cache, so a clip the hub refuses re-opens a session on every request. Absurd values fail worse: clip_path runs before async_preview_clip's try block, so an OverflowError from datetime escapes the view and aiohttp answers 500 with a stack trace. The lazy fix is one range check in the view (reject outside roughly now-400d..now+60s) rather than exact membership in coordinator.clips_for(), which would break previews for clips older than the poll window.

title: Every preview thumbnail re-fetches the whole paired-camera list from the hub instead of using the cached one
rationale: The preview view already holds the coordinator, and the coordinator caches self.cameras precisely because the call is expensive -- its own comment measures it at 58ms and refreshes it only every 300 seconds. But the view calls client.camera_at, which calls client.cameras() unconditionally, so opening a recordings card with N undownloaded clips issues N extra getGeneralDeviceList round trips on top of N media sessions, against hardware the whole codebase treats as easy to overload. Replacing camera_at with a bounds-checked coordinator.cameras[index] removes the round trip entirely; the only care needed is a fallback for the window where the cache is still empty.

title: The "Recording…" pulse mostly never appears, and when it does it lingers up to 45s after the event ended
rationale: `set hass` stores the new state map but only renders on the very first call, so the only recurring render is the 60s poll. `live` is computed at render time against a 45-second window, so a detection is shown only if a render happens to land inside those 45 seconds -- roughly one render in four, and up to 45s late. Worse, _pulseTimer is armed for 45s from the render rather than from the event, so a dot lit at t=40s stays lit until t=85s: the card claims something is recording when nothing is. The only test assigns card._hass directly and calls _render() by hand, so it verifies the markup and never the path that would trigger it. Scored below the board's impact 4 because the defect is confined to a cosmetic indicator -- no recording, download or entity state is affected.

title: attach_detections falls back to an O(clips x detections) scan on every poll
rationale: When a clip's start second is not an exact key in by_time, the code scans the whole detections dict looking for one within MATCH_SECONDS. One clip off by a second costs a full scan; a systematic one-second index drift makes the whole call quadratic, and it runs per camera on every 2-second poll over a 24-hour window. The board measured the real function at 0.31 ms for n=1000 when timestamps match exactly versus 23.46 ms when all shifted by one second (n=500: 0.16 vs 5.83 ms) -- textbook n^2. The fix is three lines with no behaviour worth arguing about: probe by_time.get(moment + delta) for delta in (-2, -1, 1, 2), which is O(1) and picks the nearest match rather than the first in insertion order.

Verified at HEAD b764e98, line numbers unchanged.

custom_components/tapo_h500/clips.py:223-225 --

            (found for when, found in by_time.items()
             if abs(when - moment) <= MATCH_SECONDS), None)

with clips.py:207 `MATCH_SECONDS = 2`.

Called once per camera per poll, coordinator.py:739 -- `attach_detections(clips, detections)` -- inside the per-camera loop, over the window built at coordinator.py:717 `window = now - LOOKBACK_SECONDS` with const.py:169 `LOOKBACK_SECONDS = 86400` and const.py:139 `DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL = 2`.

title: Auto-restart cooldown and circuit breaker live only in coordinator memory, so every Home Assistant restart re-arms an immediate hub reboot
rationale: _auto_restarted starts at 0.0 and _auto_restart_broken at False in __init__, and no Store or other persistence exists anywhere in the integration. The media handshake runs on poll 0 (0 % _media_every == 0), so on a wedged hub the very first poll after any HA start sets media_status="wedged" and `elapsed = now - 0.0` (epoch seconds) trivially clears the 6-hour cooldown, rebooting the hub immediately. A tripped breaker -- the state that exists precisely because rebooting is NOT curing the failure -- is wiped with it, so the pattern is one hub reboot per HA restart on hardware documented as fragile. Scored impact 3 rather than 4 only because the whole path is behind an opt-in option that defaults off. Note a much lazier partial fix exists: seed _auto_restarted to the construction time, which kills the immediate reboot without any Store, though it does not preserve the breaker.

                    and not self._auto_restart_broken

title: reference.md and protocol-notes.md still say doorbell presses are unidentified and RING_ALARM_TYPES is empty
rationale: const.py has shipped `RING_ALARM_TYPES: set[int] = {17}` and both limitations.md and one section of protocol-notes.md document the press as confirmed, but reference.md still tells the reader in three places that nothing classifies as a ring and that they must go find the code themselves, and protocol-notes.md contradicts its own earlier section 390 lines later. A user who reads reference.md concludes the "Doorbell presses only" download mode is a no-op and never turns it on. Fix is deleting or rewriting four stale paragraphs. title: README and reference.md quote translation keys as entity IDs for four entities that actually get name-derived IDs
rationale: Entities set _attr_has_entity_name = True, so Home Assistant slugifies the display name, not the translation key, into the entity_id. Three documented IDs therefore do not exist (one of them documented twice). The worst is the README's no-internet setup step, which is load-bearing for the project's core mission and names a switch the user cannot find. reference.md already gets the sibling switches right, including the correct `switch.*_automatic_firmware_updates` at line 39, so this is drift rather than a house convention.

title: No CI at all -- the only gate is a local script a human must remember to run, on a repo HACS installs from
rationale: tools/verify.sh is a good gate that nothing enforces. The GitHub remote is the one HACS users install from, so a push that skips the script ships to real installs unchecked. A workflow running the existing script is one file, adds no runtime behaviour to the integration and never touches the hub. Implementer caveat: `origin` is a LAN server and `github` is the mirror, so CI only runs on pushes that reach the mirror.

title: Media-session credentials are snapshotted once at connect() and never refreshed, while the control channel is documented to silently re-login across hub reboots
rationale: connect() copies superSecretKey and the encryption method off the pytapo object and is called exactly once per config-entry lifetime, while the integration explicitly relies on pytapo re-establishing the control session underneath it across reboots -- including the reboot the integration itself triggers. I read the installed pytapo 3.4.18 and can now split the claim honestly: superSecretKey is a constructor-only attribute that is never reassigned, so that half is refuted; but the encryption method resolves through the live transport and IS reassigned on re-login, so the snapshot can go stale. Decisive supporting evidence: pytapo's own getStreamSession reads both values fresh at session-open time, so the proposed one-line change (read from self._hub when opening a session) simply matches upstream and is a no-op whenever nothing rotates. Impact cut from the board's 4 to 3 accordingly.

Verified at HEAD b764e98. api.py line numbers shifted substantially in iteration 1 (180-181 -> 263-264, 529-531 -> 611-613) and __init__.py 198 -> 199.

Captured once, custom_components/tapo_h500/api.py:263-264 (inside connect(), which begins at api.py:229) --
        self._super_secret_key = self._hub.superSecretKey
        self._encryption_method = self._hub.getEncryptionMethod()

Used for every session thereafter, api.py:611-613 --
                session = H500MediaSession(
                    ip=self.host, cloud_password=self.cloud_password,
                    super_secret_key=self._super_secret_key,
                    encryptionMethod=self._encryption_method, port=8800,

Only caller of connect(), custom_components/tapo_h500/__init__.py:199 -- `await hass.async_add_executor_job(client.connect)`

NEW evidence from the installed library (read-only, no network):
- .venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pytapo/__init__.py:99 is the ONLY assignment to self.superSecretKey -- it cannot rotate. This half of the board's claim is wrong.
- pytapo/__init__.py:148-149 `def getEncryptionMethod(self): return self.transport.getEncryptionMethod()` -- a live read, not a stored value.
- pytapo/transport/pytapo/pytapo.py:190-191 returns self.passwordEncryptionMethod, which IS reassigned repeatedly: reset to None at :209 and :487, re-derived at :507 (SHA256) / :509 (MD5), and forced to MD5 at :718. So a re-login can change it under the integration's snapshot.
- pytapo/__init__.py:319-326 getStreamSession passes `self.superSecretKey, self.getEncryptionMethod()` freshly on every session -- upstream already does what this candidate proposes.

The reboot-survives-underneath assumption, button.py:57-60. The symptom it would produce, coordinator.py:132-135 ("every session works and carries nothing, for every clip, until a reboot").

title: A failed automatic download is never retried, so the hub's own documented media outage permanently loses that footage
rationale: _download_new marks every clip seen in _seen_clips BEFORE spawning the download, and only one of the three failure branches un-marks it. EmptyRecordingError and HomeAssistantError both `return` after bumping a counter, leaving the (start_time,) key in _seen_clips, which is only ever pruned at window - LOOKBACK_SECONDS (48h) -- by which time the clip has left the hub's 24h index anyway. So a clip that failed to download is never offered again. This is not a rare path: media.py's own EmptyRecordingError docstring documents a hub state where EVERY session answers zero bytes until a reboot, and the coordinator goes to the length of rebooting the hub itself to cure it -- then never re-fetches a single clip it lost, even though the hub still holds the recordings for days. The author already applied exactly this reasoning one level over, to frames, in note_served_download: 'Every clip during the outage burned its one frame-fetch attempt on an empty answer. Clearing the marks lets the camera picture repair itself.' The same clear was not done for _seen_clips. The verify-failure branch proves the mechanism is understood and cheap -- one .discard() line. tests/test_download_watch.py exercises both failure branches and asserts only on download_failures, so nothing pins the current no-retry behaviour.

title: Card and notification downloads write no usable sidecar, so every manually saved clip is invisible to the by-type browser and to find_face -- permanently
rationale: The sidecar JSON is the only durable record of what a clip was and who was in it once the hub's one-day index rolls over; both the media browser's by-type folders and find_face's archive half read nothing else. The automatic path passes detected= AND faces=. The service path never passes faces= at all, and populates detected only in the branch where the caller omitted end_time. The Lovelace card always sends both start_time and end_time, so every card-initiated download takes `detected == []` -> `detected or None` -> no sidecar written whatsoever. The notification 'Save' button omits end_time, so it does write a sidecar -- with detection_types and no face_ids -- and async_classify_downloads can never repair that one, because its `missing` filter only considers clips with NO .json at all. Net effect: the clips a person deliberately saved are exactly the ones find_face can never find, and the by-type folders silently show only what downloaded itself. The clip record needed to fix this is already in hand (the end_time branch has it; the other branch can read it free from coordinator.clips_for(camera_index)), so no extra hub call is involved.

title: "Keep the newest N doorbell presses however old they get" only protects clips still inside the hub's 24-hour index
rationale: _protected builds the keep-set from self.clips_for(index), which is the polled window -- _poll asks the hub for `now - LOOKBACK_SECONDS` and LOOKBACK_SECONDS is 86400. async_prune, by contrast, deletes across the whole on-disk archive (_videos globs */* under the camera directory, which is months of day folders). So a doorbell press is protected for the 24 hours it stays in the hub's index and is then indistinguishable from motion: as soon as it drops out of the window it becomes prunable and gets deleted the moment it falls past the newest CONF_KEEP_DOWNLOADS files. That is precisely the failure the option was added to prevent, and both docstrings assert the opposite in the same words -- _protected says 'however old they get' and newest_matching says 'What retention must leave alone however old it gets'. Reachable whenever CONF_KEEP_DOWNLOADS > 0 and CONF_KEEP_RINGS (or CONF_KEEP_PERSON) > 0; both are ordinary 0-500 fields on the Configure page. The on-disk sidecars already carry detection_types, so the durable fix is to protect from disk rather than from the poll window -- which is the same root cause as correctness-i2-2 and should probably be fixed after it.

title: The contact-sheet image never goes unavailable and never re-stamps at local midnight, so it serves a 500 every quiet morning
rationale: H500ContactSheet.async_image builds the sheet for today's LOCAL date and returns None when that folder holds no thumbnails, but the class overrides no `available` property -- so the docstring's claim that it is 'Unavailable on a quiet day' is not implemented. Home Assistant's image view turns a None from async_image into HTTPInternalServerError, so the dashboard tile is a broken image rather than an unavailable entity. Worse, image_last_updated is stamped only by the signal("image") dispatcher, which fires exactly once per successful automatic download (coordinator.py:1136). Nothing fires at local midnight, so from midnight until the first download of the new day the entity's state still points at yesterday and any fetch 500s -- every night on every camera, and all day on a camera that sees nobody. Its sibling H500EventImage avoids this by also subscribing to the event signal; the contact sheet subscribes only to the download one, and the comment explaining that choice never considered the day boundary.

custom_components/tapo_h500/image.py:104-105 -- the claim:
    Unavailable on a quiet day rather than showing a blank sheet, which would
    read as a fault.

custom_components/tapo_h500/image.py:132-139 -- but None is returned and no `available` is defined anywhere in the class:
    async def async_image(self) -> bytes | None:

        # only when image_last_updated changes, so this runs about as often as
        # a clip arrives ...
        return await async_contact_sheet(
            self.hass, self.camera,
            dt_util.as_local(dt_util.utcnow()).date().isoformat())

            self.hass, self.coordinator.signal("image", self.index),

title: restore_names validates the keys of `settings` and none of the values, writing arbitrary shapes straight into the config entry's options
rationale: RESTORE_SCHEMA opens with a comment naming exactly this hazard -- 'a restore is exactly the moment somebody pastes a hand-edited blob in: an id that is not a string or a rank that is not a number would sit there until something else tripped over it, a long way from here' -- and then enforces it for face_names and camera_order but declares settings as {cv.string: object}. merge_settings filters keys against USER_OPTIONS and passes every value through untouched into restored_options, which writes the whole mapping to the entry. The 'long way from here' failures are concrete: CONF_DOWNLOAD_TYPES as the string "17" iterates per character and silently becomes the filter {1, 7}, so downloads quietly stop matching anything; CONF_SENSITIVITY as anything but a mapping makes coordinator.sensitivity raise AttributeError inside an entity property, breaking every unusual-activity and activity-level state write; CONF_KEEP_DOWNLOADS as a string raises TypeError at `if keep <= 0` inside the background download task, so pruning silently stops. The types are already declared once in the options schema (config_flow.py:386-397), so the fix is reusing those validators rather than inventing new ones.
evidence:
custom_components/tapo_h500/__init__.py:129-140 -- the stated principle, then the exemption:
# Validated rather than trusted. This writes straight into the config entry's
# options, and a restore is exactly the moment somebody pastes a hand-edited
# blob in: an id that is not a string or a rank that is not a number would sit
# there until something else tripped over it, a long way from here.
RESTORE_SCHEMA = vol.Schema({
    vol.Required("config_entry_id"): cv.string,
    vol.Required("face_names"): vol.Schema({cv.string: cv.string}),
    vol.Optional("camera_order"): vol.Schema({
        cv.string: vol.All(vol.Coerce(int), vol.Range(min=0, max=20))}),
    # The authored settings, filtered to the known keys again at merge time
    # -- a restore is exactly the moment somebody pastes a hand-edited blob.
    vol.Optional("settings"): vol.Schema({cv.string: object}),

custom_components/tapo_h500/backup.py:98-102 -- keys filtered, values passed through:
    merged = dict(current)
    if incoming:
        merged.update({key: value for key, value in incoming.items()
                       if key in USER_OPTIONS})
    return merged

the silently-wrong site, custom_components/tapo_h500/coordinator.py:956-962:

        for value in self.entry.options.get(CONF_DOWNLOAD_TYPES) or []:
            try:

title: AUTH_ERROR_CODES contains -40209, which this repo documents fifteen times as "exists, wrong params" — so the one live reauth trigger fires on a shape mismatch and permanently ends retries
rationale: Iteration 1's own commit message names the single live route to H500AuthError: "The one live route is a coded refusal out of Tapo.__init__'s own getBasicInfo call." That call is a getter with a params shape, and -40209 is exactly this hub's answer to a getter called with the wrong shape — protocol-notes.md establishes that rule twice and uses it as the discriminator that proved the face and battery methods absent. It is also the siren's volume-range rejection, cited in five separate modules. So the classifier's only reachable trigger is dominated by a code that means "wrong parameters", not "wrong password". When it fires, __init__.py raises ConfigEntryAuthFailed, HA stops retrying, and the owner gets a reauth form for a password that was never wrong — the precise fail-dangerous direction is_auth_failure's docstring exists to forbid ("Fails safe towards RETRY, and that direction is the whole point... put a 'check your password' notification in front of somebody whose password is fine"). The other two members, -40414 and -40418, appear nowhere else in the repo or in docs/protocol-notes.md, a file that otherwise records every code observed on hardware; so the set has no protocol evidence for two of its members and contradicting evidence for the third. This is NOT the documented backlog limitation ("the trigger may never fire") — it is the opposite failure: the trigger firing on the wrong stimulus. The lazy fix is to delete -40209 from the frozenset, which only widens retry.
evidence:
custom_components/tapo_h500/api.py:131 —
AUTH_ERROR_CODES = frozenset({-40209, -40414, -40418})

What the repo's own protocol work says -40209 means, docs/protocol-notes.md:130-133 —
That uniformity is the evidence. Every method on this hub that exists but is
being called wrongly answers `-40209` or `-40211` — that is how the face
detection setter and the mirrorscreen shape were both found. Not one such reply
appeared here, so these methods are absent rather than merely mis-shaped.

and docs/protocol-notes.md:170-171 —
`-40106`, with none of the `-40209`/`-40211` replies that mean "exists, wrong
params".

and docs/protocol-notes.md:673 —
| `setSirenConfig` | `{"siren":{"volume":"8",…}}` | accepted; volume **1-10**, 0 and 11 give `-40209` |

The contract it breaks, custom_components/tapo_h500/api.py:166-171 —
    Fails safe towards RETRY, and that direction is the whole point. This hub
    wedges under repeated logins and recovers only on a timeout; a wedge
    surfaces as a reset, a timeout or a zero-byte read, none of which carries
    a code. Calling one of those an auth failure would end the retries and
    put a "check your password" notification in front of somebody whose
    password is fine.

The consequence, custom_components/tapo_h500/__init__.py:200-205 —
    except H500AuthError as err:
        await hass.async_add_executor_job(client.close)
        raise ConfigEntryAuthFailed(
            "The H500 refused the stored credentials") from err

And the only live trigger, quoted from the iteration-1 commit b30d1d9 message:
"The one live route is a coded refusal out of Tapo.__init__'s own getBasicInfo
call, and that is asserted, not demonstrated on hardware."

`grep -rn -- "-40414\|-40418" custom_components/ docs/ tests/` returns exactly one line: api.py:131 itself.

title: A failed automatic download is never retried, so every clip recorded during a wedge or an outage is lost permanently even though the hub still holds it for 24 hours
rationale: _fresh marks a clip's start time in _seen_clips the moment it is considered, and _download's two failure paths (EmptyRecordingError and HomeAssistantError) return without un-marking it. The corrupt-file path four lines below does un-mark, so the mechanism for a retry is present and used — just not on the paths that actually fire during a hub failure. Consequence: on a hub in the known serving-empty state, or during any outage where sessions fail, every fresh clip burns its one and only download attempt. The hub's clip index holds 24 hours; _fresh's own pruning keeps the seen key for 48, so the key outlives the clip and the download can never happen. When the hub recovers, the archive has a hole exactly covering the failure window — which is the footage most likely to be wanted afterwards. The author already reasoned through this exact problem for the other one-attempt-per-clip resource and fixed it there: note_served_download clears _frame_attempts on recovery with the comment "Every clip during the outage burned its one frame-fetch attempt on an empty answer. Clearing the marks lets the camera picture repair itself." The same sentence is true of downloads, and _seen_clips is not cleared. Fixing it in the same hook is the small diff and adds no sessions while the hub is still failing, which keeps it clear of the board's offline-4 concern.
evidence:
custom_components/tapo_h500/coordinator.py:1100-1112 — both failure paths return with the clip still marked seen:
        except EmptyRecordingError as err:
            _LOGGER.warning("Automatic download of clip %s failed: %s",
                            start_time, err)
            self._download_failures[index] = (
                self._download_failures.get(index, 0) + 1)
            self.note_empty_download()
            return
        except HomeAssistantError as err:
            _LOGGER.warning("Automatic download of clip %s failed: %s",
                            start_time, err)
            self._download_failures[index] = (
                self._download_failures.get(index, 0) + 1)
            return

The un-marking that does exist, four lines later, custom_components/tapo_h500/coordinator.py:1123 —
            self._seen_clips.get(index, set()).discard((start_time,))

The recovery hook that clears the sibling resource but not this one, custom_components/tapo_h500/coordinator.py:992-999 —
        if recovering:
            # Every clip during the outage burned its one frame-fetch
            # attempt on an empty answer. Clearing the marks lets the
            # camera picture repair itself at the next look instead of
            # staying stale until the next event. Only on recovery: a
            # routine download clearing them would invite a redundant
            # refetch per clip.
            self._frame_attempts.clear()

Why the key outlives the clip — custom_components/tapo_h500/coordinator.py:937-939 prunes at 48h:
        seen_map[index] = {
            k for k in seen if k[0] >= window - LOOKBACK_SECONDS}

while the hub is only asked about the last 24h, custom_components/tapo_h500/coordinator.py:716-717 with const.py:169 LOOKBACK_SECONDS = 86400:
        now = int(dt_util.utcnow().timestamp())
        window = now - LOOKBACK_SECONDS

title: The media lock is held across an unbounded session handshake, and both wedge probes are gated off exactly while it is held, so one stalled session blinds the detector and freezes the media path until a reload
rationale: iter_recording takes the client's single asyncio.Lock with no timeout, then enters the session context manager — the TCP connect, digest challenge and AES key exchange — with no asyncio.wait_for around it. Only the per-packet read below it is bounded, at 35 seconds, which shows the author bounded the part they were thinking about and not the part before it. api.py's own check_media_port classifies and names the hub state that produces a stalled handshake: "silent" is returned when the port accepts a connection and then says nothing past the timeout. In that state the lock is pinned indefinitely, and the coordinator's two wedge probes are both explicitly skipped while lock.locked() — so media_status and _media_evidence freeze at whatever they last said, the auto-restart's `reason` can never become "wedged" or "empty", and the self-healing path built for exactly this hardware never fires. Meanwhile every later iter_recording queues behind the same lock with no timeout: the per-clip auto-downloads, async_latest_frame called from H500Camera.async_camera_image, and H500PreviewView.get, which is an aiohttp request handler that will simply never answer. Nothing in the process recovers this; only reloading the entry or restarting Home Assistant does. This is a different mechanism from board item offline-4 (session volume) and a different fix: a total deadline on the session, or a bounded lock acquisition for the decorative callers.

The hub state that produces a stalled handshake is named by this module, custom_components/tapo_h500/api.py:119-120:
    except (socket.timeout, TimeoutError):
        return "silent"

        if (check is not None and self._polls % self._media_every == 0

title: The camera-list refresh is gated on a poll counter that only advances on a successful poll, so the list can never be re-read while polls are failing
rationale: _polls += 1 sits at the very end of _poll, after the per-camera activity fetch that raises UpdateFailed. The camera-list refresh at the top of _poll is gated on `self._polls % self._cameras_every == 0`. So the moment the activity fetch starts failing, _polls freezes and the gate can only be true if it happened to be true already — meaning the five-minute refresh is silently disabled for the entire duration of any outage. I demonstrated this offline against the repo's own harness: after one good poll and forty consecutive failing polls, client.cameras() had been called exactly once and _polls was still 1. The always-true consequence is mild (a camera paired or unpaired while the hub was down stays wrong for a while after recovery). The sharp one is a deadlock: if the failure is CAUSED by the stale list — a removed or re-paired camera whose device_id the hub now refuses, which activity() surfaces as `raise RuntimeError(f"searchVideoWithUTC failed ({...})")` — then refreshing the list is the only cure and it is gated behind a counter that the failure itself has frozen. The integration stays dead at a 300-second backoff until someone reloads the entry. The tests never reach this: every backoff and camera-list test fails at client.cameras itself, and the one refresh test has to write `coord._polls = 0` by hand to make the gate open.

            except Exception as err:
                raise UpdateFailed(f"Could not poll H500 activity: {err}") from err

title: A Home Assistant restart mid-download leaks a .part temp file into the media archive that nothing ever sweeps, and no lister, browser or retention pass can see it
rationale: _make_temp writes the in-progress download straight into the clip's own <camera>/<date>/ folder with a .part suffix, and the only thing that deletes it is `temporary.unlink(True)` in the coroutine's own finally clause — which does not run when the process dies. Home Assistant restarts for every core update, every add-on change and every host reboot, and with auto-download on a busy camera there is usually a download in flight. Each such restart leaves an orphan of up to a full clip's size. Because Path(".tapo-h500-abc.ts.part").suffix is ".part", it is invisible to _videos (so async_prune never counts or deletes it), invisible to media_source's MIME_TYPES filter (so it never appears in the browser), and invisible to the contact sheet and latest-image scans. There is no startup sweep anywhere: grep for ".part" across the component returns only the three _make_temp call sites and one const comment. So it is unbounded, silent growth on the Home Assistant disk. async_preview_clip makes one too, so a restart during a card browse leaks as well. The fix is one age-bounded glob("*/*.part") at setup — age-bounded specifically so it cannot delete a download in flight.
evidence:
custom_components/tapo_h500/media.py:127-131 — the temp file lands in the archive folder itself:
def _make_temp(parent: Path, suffix: str) -> tuple[int, Path]:
    parent.mkdir(mode=0o755, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    descriptor, name = tempfile.mkstemp(
        prefix=".tapo-h500-", suffix=suffix, dir=parent)
    return descriptor, Path(name)

custom_components/tapo_h500/media.py:227-228 (download) and :175-176 (preview):
    descriptor, temporary = await hass.async_add_executor_job(
        _make_temp, target.parent, ".ts.part")

    finally:
        if stream is not None:
            await hass.async_add_executor_job(stream.close)
        await hass.async_add_executor_job(temporary.unlink, True)

    # Names sort chronologically: <date>/<HHMMSS>.<ext>.
    return sorted(path for path in directory.glob("*/*")

    videos = await hass.async_add_executor_job(_videos, camera_dir(hass, camera))

No sweep exists: `grep -rn "\.part" custom_components/tapo_h500/*.py` returns only media.py:176, media.py:228, media.py:242 and the const.py:577 comment.

title: _load() has no request/response correlation, so a camera or day change either does nothing or lands the previous selection's clips under the new label
rationale: Two separate holes in one path. First, _load() early-returns while _busy, so the reload that the camera picker and the day pager queue up right after their own _render() silently does nothing if the 60-second poll (or the initial load) is still in flight — the card is left showing "Loading recordings..." until the next tick, because _recordings was just nulled. Second, and worse, the in-flight response was built from the OLD this._index and this._window(), and _load() applies _days/_camera/_cameras/_recordings unconditionally when it lands. So the user clicks "previous day", the earlier request returns, and today's clips are rendered under yesterday's pager label; click a second camera and camera 1's clips render with the picker highlighting camera 2 (the title comes from response.camera, so header and highlight disagree too). The window is real: list_recordings is a searchVideoWithUTC plus a detections sweep, both queued behind the client's _hub_lock while a 2-second coordinator poll uses the same lock. The lazy fix is one generation counter — `const token = ++this._token` before the await, `if (token !== this._token) return;` before the assignments — plus letting a user-initiated load supersede rather than early-return. Overlap disclosure: board frontend-cards-3 mentions the `_busy` early-return in passing as the reason Refresh stays disabled; it does not cover the stale-response application, which is a data-correctness bug with a different fix.

title: Every row's Play/Delete/Download button has the same accessible name, and Delete fires immediately with no confirmation
rationale: _actions() is shared by the list, hero, timeline and (via _row/_event) every clip row, and it emits buttons whose entire accessible name is the literal word "Play", "Delete" or "Download". The time that identifies the clip lives in a sibling div (.when) with no aria-labelledby tying it to the buttons, so a screen-reader user tabbing a forty-clip list hears "Delete button" forty times with nothing distinguishing them — WCAG 2.4.6 in the plainest form. The destructive one is the one with no name and no guard: the delete branch calls the service straight from the click, while the far less consequential rename path already stops for a window.prompt. Note the honest limit on severity: delete_recording removes only the downloaded copy (async_delete_clip takes no client), so it is re-downloadable — unless the hub's loop recording has already rotated the clip away, in which case it is gone. Fix is cheap and local: an esc'd aria-label carrying the clip's own timestamp on each of the three buttons, and a window.confirm in the delete branch matching the prompt idiom already in the file. Distinct from board frontend-cards-4 (focus destroyed by re-render) and -5 (live region never announces).

title: One failed service call throws away a listing that is still in memory and replaces the whole card body with a raw exception string
rationale: _render() treats _error as an alternative to the body rather than as something shown beside it, so any failure blanks the list, the pager and the chips — even though this._recordings still holds the last good result and was never touched by the failure. The trigger is not exotic: _onClick's catch fires for every action, so deleting a clip whose local copy has already gone shows "No downloaded copy of that recording was found" where forty rows used to be, and the hub this integration exists for is documented to wedge and refuse connections. Recovery needs a Refresh click or up to 60 s of waiting, because _error is only cleared by a successful _load(). The div also has no role="alert", so a screen reader is told nothing at all — the card just goes quiet. Fix: render the error as a banner above the body, keep the body when _recordings is non-null, add role="alert". Related but distinct from board tests-5, which asks for coverage of this render; the defect here is the behaviour itself, and covering it without changing it would pin the wrong thing.

title: Naming a face forces a full hub re-listing to learn a name the card just typed, justified by a comment describing a reload that no longer happens
rationale: The name branch awaits _load() after name_face, and the comment above it explains why: "the name lives on the config entry, so Home Assistant reloads the integration; reloading the list is what picks the new name up." That reload was deliberately removed on the Python side — _async_options_changed now detects a face-names-only change and returns after a dispatcher signal, with a comment naming this exact card behaviour as the harm it was fixing. So the card pays a searchVideoWithUTC plus a detections sweep against the hub, and the user waits for it, purely to read back a string the card already holds; name_face's own response even returns {face_id, name, named}. The lazy fix is three lines in the name branch: patch this._sharedNames from the answer (delete the key when it is empty, matching the service) and _render(), no reload. The stale comment goes with it. Scoped to the name path only — the download and delete branches genuinely need the re-listing to refresh `downloaded`, `thumbnail` and `url`.

title: The 60-second poll never checks document.hidden, so a background tab or a wall tablet keeps asking the hub for a 7-day clip search forever
rationale: connectedCallback arms an unconditional setInterval and nothing in the file consults document.hidden or visibilitychange (verified by grep at HEAD). A browser tab left open on a dashboard, or a wall tablet showing a different view, keeps issuing list_recordings for every card on the page for as long as the page lives — each one a searchVideoWithUTC over the card's whole window plus a detections sweep, taken under the same client _hub_lock the 2-second event poller uses, so it also delays that poller for its duration. Being honest about the ceiling: with the coordinator already polling at 2 s by default, this is not a large share of total hub traffic, so the win is the heavier serialized call disappearing while nobody is looking, not a dramatic load reduction. The fix is native and about four lines — return early from the tick when document.hidden, and do one _load() on the visible transition so the card is fresh when it comes back — with no new dependency and nothing new contacted.
